Naujan_Location: Naujan is a 1st Class Municipality in the Philippines, known for agriculture and tourism on Mindoro Island.
Naujan is located on the northeastern part of Mindoro Island in the Philippines.

Naujan_Lake_About: Naujan Lake National Park covers about 20,000 hectares and is the 5th largest freshwater lake in the Philippines. It was designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 1999, recognizing its critical importance for migratory birds.

The lake hosts over 60 species of birds, including endangered species like the Philippine duck (Anas luzonica). During the migration season (November-March), thousands of Siberian birds visit the lake.

Eco-tourism activities at Naujan Lake include birdwatching, boat tours, photography, and nature walks. Best time to visit: November to March for birdwatching. Contact the Naujan LGU at (043) 208-3382 for guided tours.

Mangyan_Culture: Mangyan communities in Naujan: Several Mangyan indigenous groups (mainly Iraya and Alangan tribes) live in the upland and forested barangays of Naujan. They are known for handwoven rattan and abaca baskets, traditional jewelry, and the ambahan â€” a form of pre-colonial poetry still practiced today. Some communities engage in sustainable farming of root crops and wild herbs.

To visit Mangyan communities in Naujan responsibly:
â€¢ Always arrange visits through the Naujan LGU or a certified community guide
â€¢ Do NOT enter communities unannounced or without permission
â€¢ Purchasing Mangyan crafts directly supports their livelihood
â€¢ Avoid photography without asking permission first
â€¢ The Hanunuo Mangyan script (a pre-colonial writing system) is still taught within communities â€” it is a UNESCO-recognized intangible cultural heritage of the Philippines.

Mangyan handicrafts available in Naujan area: woven baskets (rattan and abaca), decorative bags, traditional jewelry, and abaca cloth. Look for certified fair-trade sellers to ensure artisans receive fair compensation.

Agriculture_Crops: Naujan's main agricultural products are rice (palay) and coconut (copra). Rice is typically harvested from November-December, while coconut farming is year-round. The municipality also produces corn, bananas, root crops, and vegetables.

The rice paddies of Naujan cover thousands of hectares. The best time to see the green rice fields is June-September. During harvest season (October-November), you can see the golden rice ready for harvest.

Coconut farming is a major livelihood in Naujan. Copra (dried coconut kernel) is processed for coconut oil and other products. Some farmers also engage in mixed farming with vegetables and root crops.

Naujan_Overview: Naujan is a 1st Class Municipality in the Philippines, famous for Naujan Lake National Park – the 5th largest lake in the Philippines and a RAMSAR Wetland of International Importance. It is also home to rich agriculture (rice and coconut), Mangyan indigenous communities, and warm, hospitable people.

Naujan offers: Naujan Lake National Park (birdwatching, eco-tours, boating), heritage sites like Naujan Church, thriving rice and coconut farms, Mangyan cultural heritage, and serene river ecosystems like Sadya River. It is a peaceful and scenic destination away from crowded tourist areas.

Key facts about Naujan: 1st Class Municipality in the Philippines located on Mindoro Island. Population 100,000+. Main industries: rice farming, coconut/copra, fishing, and eco-tourism. Known for agriculture and tourism. The municipality borders Calapan to the northwest and is about 30-45 minutes by van from Calapan Port.
Transportation_How_To_Get_There:
How to get to Naujan from Manila:
1. From Manila: Take a bus (Buendia or EDSA terminals) to Batangas Pier (~2 hours).
2. Take a ferry from Batangas Pier to Calapan Port:
   - Fastcraft: ~1 hour (₱280–₱350)
   - RORO ferry: ~3 hours (₱150–₱200)
   - Ferry companies: Montenegro Lines, Starlite Ferries, ATSC
3. From Calapan Port: Take a jeepney or van to Naujan (~30–45 minutes, ₱40–₱80).
Van/jeepney terminals in Calapan City serve Naujan regularly.

Step-by-step from Manila:
Manila → Batangas Pier (bus, ~2 hrs) → Calapan Port (ferry, ~1–3 hrs) → Naujan (jeepney/van, ~30–45 min).
Total travel time from Manila: approximately 4–6 hours depending on ferry schedule. Tip: Book the morning ferry (6–7 AM departure) from Batangas to arrive in Naujan before noon.

Nearest transport hub to Naujan is Calapan City, just 30–45 minutes away. From Calapan, jeepneys and vans regularly serve Naujan. The van terminal in Calapan is near the port area. Fare is approximately ₱40–₱80.

• Jeepney – connects Naujan to Calapan and nearby towns
• Van for hire – best for day tours around Naujan Lake and nearby areas

The national highway passes through Naujan, making it easy to flag down transport.

From Naujan Poblacion to Naujan Lake: approximately 15–25 minutes by tricycle or habal-habal. Hire a local guide or boat operator at the lake's shoreline for tours. For trips to nearby barangays, habal-habal is the most practical option. Jeepney/van rides back to Calapan leave from the town proper.

Best_Time_To_Visit:

• November–March – BEST for birdwatching at Naujan Lake: migratory birds from Siberia and East Asia arrive
• December–February – coolest and most comfortable months for outdoor activities
• June–October – rainy/typhoon season; the rice fields are lush and green, but travel may be disrupted
Tip: Visit early morning (5–8 AM) year-round for the best birdwatching experience at the lake.

Naujan travel seasons:

• Habagat (southwest monsoon, June–Oct): rainy season – rice paddies are vivid green but typhoons are possible
• Peak bird migration: November to March – Philippine Ducks, Spotted Whistling Ducks, and Siberian migratory birds
• Town Fiesta: September 8 – a great time to experience local culture even during the wet season

History_Heritage:
History of Naujan:
Naujan is one of the oldest settlements in Naujan. The municipality was established during the Spanish colonial period. The Our Lady of the Nativity Parish Church (Naujan Church) is a historic landmark that has served as the spiritual center of the community for centuries. During World War II, the Battle of Mindoro took place nearby as American forces liberated the island from Japanese occupation in December 1944â€“January 1945.

Heritage sites in Naujan:
â€¢ Naujan Church (Our Lady of the Nativity Parish) â€” built during the Spanish colonial era, a cornerstone of the town's identity and still an active parish
â€¢ Naujan Town Plaza â€” the historic center of the municipality
â€¢ Naujan Lake National Park â€” declared a national park and RAMSAR wetland site, protecting the lake's ecological and cultural significance
â€¢ Mangyan cultural communities in the upland barangays â€” living heritage of pre-colonial culture

Naujan Lake has been central to the community's livelihood for generations â€” local fishermen have depended on it for centuries. The lake was declared a RAMSAR Wetland of International Importance in 1999, recognizing its global ecological significance. The Mangyan people have inhabited the Mindoro interior (including Naujan's uplands) for over 2,000 years before Spanish colonization.
Naujan_Lake_Wildlife: Naujan Lake National Park is a RAMSAR wetland site and one of the Philippines' most important bird sanctuaries. It hosts over 100 bird species including the critically endangered Philippine Duck (Anas luzonica) and the Spotted Whistling Duck. The lake is also home to freshwater crocodiles, sea turtles (nesting on nearby shores), monitor lizards, and diverse fish species.

Naujan Lake biodiversity: The lake covers 20,000+ hectares and supports migratory birds from Siberia and other parts of Asia every Novemberâ€“March. Endemic birds include the Ashy Ground Thrush and various herons and egrets. Guided birdwatching tours can be arranged through the Naujan LGU and park rangers.

Naujan_Lake_National_Park: Naujan Lake National Park is the fifth largest lake in the Philippines, surrounded by lush mountains and rich biodiversity. The ambiance is calm, serene, and peaceful. Simbahang_Bato: Simbahang Bato (Bancuro Ruins) is a historic 17th-century coral and adobe church ruin with a unique 'church within a church' design. The moss-covered walls and open-air structures create a hauntingly beautiful atmosphere where history and faith meet. Visitors can explore the ruins, take photos, learn about Spanish-era heritage, and feel the quiet reverence of this iconic site in Brgy. Bancuro, Naujan.

• Karacha Falls (Brgy. Malvar) - majestic waterfall with strong cascading waters and deep pool. Activities: off-road trekking, swimming in refreshing pool, forest exploration, photography
• ORIC sa Bathala Waterfalls (Sitio Bathala) - emerging eco-tourism destination with thrilling hanging bridge and horseback access to falls. Activities: hanging bridge crossing, horseback riding, swimming in cool waters
All waterfalls have natural pools perfect for refreshing swims!

Naujan_Best_Activities:
Best Activities & Experiences in Naujan:
• Birdwatching at Naujan Lake National Park (over 100 bird species, especially Nov-Apr)
• Boat rides on calm, serene Naujan Lake with stunning sunset views
• Exploring historic Simbahang Bato ruins and learning Spanish-era heritage
• Nature photography at Dao Waterlily Park and various eco-parks
• Waterfall trekking and swimming at Montelago, Karacha, and Bathala Falls
• Organic farming workshops at AgriGold Farm and DJMV Organic Healing Park
• Beach swimming and relaxation at Celeste, Nabul, and Emerald Resorts
• Horseback riding at Benilda ng Bancuro Resort
• Peaceful plaza strolls at Liwasang Bonifacio
• Farm-to-table dining and local cuisine experiences
• Wellness and relaxation at hot springs and healing parks
Naujan offers perfect blend of nature, heritage, and rural charm!
